A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same OpenDPR work and support direct comparison of all supplied content. Neither contains an appendix; both reference separate supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original OpenDPR and OpenDPR-W experiments on four datasets, component ablations, error attribution, and prototype sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and analyses in Tables 1–6 and Figures 1, 4, and 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical prototype construction, visual retrieval, S2C training, and OpenDPR-W inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate building change detection on LEVIR-CD and WHU-CD and semantic change detection on Hi-UCD mini and SECOND. Table 3's Ground-to-Grass correction matches the existing Figure 4 legend and does not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–4, including I-M-C, M-C-I, and the single-prompt and multiple-prompt M-C-I variants in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same evaluation metrics, supervision and inference settings, validation selection, and training configuration, including batch size 8 and 10,000 iterations.

E4.justification: The error attribution in Figure 1, qualitative examples in Figure 4, component ablations in Tables 5–6, and prototype sensitivity analysis in Figure 5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical values, rankings, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged. Table 3 only corrects a class heading; for example, the corresponding per-class OpenDPR scores remain 26.6 IoU and 42.1 F1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and their associated mathematical definitions and reasoning are identical. No theoretical results or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about identification bottlenecks, visual prototype retrieval, S2C, and experimental superiority.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the category-identification bottleneck and the attribution of failures on rare categories such as pedestrian bridges to semantic biases in prototype construction.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, model choices, and the code repository link are identical. Neither version adds supplementary implementation material within the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions, research positioning, and all 53 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes, and Table 3's class terminology changes from Ground to Grass. The remaining wording and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Table 3's second category heading changes from Ground to Grass. Its structure, formatting, and values remain identical, as do all other figures, tables, and page layouts apart from the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 3's Ground heading to Grass resolves an inconsistency with the Hi-UCD mini legend already present in Figure 4 and clarifies which class the scores describe. This is a limited reporting improvement; the scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
